witness.text:
Your federal tax bill
on $90,000 in dividend income comes to
roughly $13,500

comparisons.rationale: On the video's own facts, taxable income is $74,250; the first $49,450 is in the 0% qualified-dividend bracket, leaving $24,800 at 15% = $3,720, not $13,500 (15% of the gross, which also contradicts its own "15% on the taxable portion" = $11,138). It also treats all $90,000 as qualified dividends and, if the 20% covered-call sleeve pays mostly non-qualified distributions (not verified against fund documents), more of it would be taxed at ordinary or 60/40 rates, and it mixes the 2025 standard deduction ($15,750) with the 2026 0% threshold ($49,450; the 2026 deduction is $16,100).

financial_checks.claim: $800/month (then $1,200 from year 3) plus $10,000 starting capital reaches $2.25 million in 11 years
financial_checks.result: CONTRADICTED: contributions total $158,800; the implied annual return is about 36.8% nominal (about 44% effective). At 3%, 7%, 10% and 14% the balance is $188K, $240K, $291K and $380K.
All equal a 4% yield; consistent with the "blended yield toward 4%", though SCHD was quoted at 3.3%.
About $49,000-$52,000 at 7-10% on the stated contributions; plausible.

financial_checks.claim: 4% raise is "about 90 extra dollars a month"; transfer raised from $800 to $1,200
financial_checks.result: 4% of $58,000 is $193/month gross (about $155 net); the transfer increases by $400.

financial_checks.claim: Federal tax on $90,000 of qualified dividends is "roughly $13,500"; take-home about $76,500
financial_checks.result: CONTRADICTED: taxable $74,250; 0% on the first $49,450, 15% on $24,800 = $3,720; take-home about $86,280 before state tax and before any non-qualified portion. The video's own stated method gives $11,138.

financial_checks.claim: 2026 single standard deduction $15,750 and 0% bracket up to $49,450
financial_checks.result: Secondary summaries of Rev. Proc. 2025-32: 2026 standard deduction $16,100 and 0% ceiling $49,450 (single); $15,750 was the 2025 deduction. Years are mixed in the video.

financial_checks.claim: No FICA on passive dividend income
financial_checks.result: Correct in general; not re-verified. (Net investment income tax is below its $200,000 threshold here.)

financial_checks.claim: SPYI/QQQI use Section 1256 index options (60% long-term / 40% short-term); return of capital "is a tax deferral mechanism" and "principal stays intact"; 3M cut a 66-year dividend streak; covered-call yields of 7-8% and 14%
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified. Return of capital lowers cost basis and is not by itself proof that NAV is preserved; the 3M streak length (65 or 66 years) and the funds' current yields should be checked.

strengths: Strong sensory opening and a coherent spine.
Genuine risk education: check NAV history before yield, return-of-capital explanation, position sizing (20% in covered-call funds).
Plain-language definitions of dividend, yield and NAV.
weaknesses: Headline outcome needs a ~37% annual return; no return assumption stated.
Tax section is wrong by a factor of about 3.6 on its own facts and mixes tax years.
Fund tickers misattributed in the key yield passage.
No channel CTA, no disclaimer, production-script leak in the narration.
contradictions: Thumbnail penthouse versus "You didn't buy a penthouse" and "The apartment is the same".
"15% on the taxable portion" ($11,138) versus "$13,500" (15% of the gross).
"$90 extra a month" versus a $400 increase "disappears entirely" into the transfer.
"Median" at 29 is $58,000 versus "current national median" $64,220 (a different population; not reconciled).
Cadence wording mixes "every week", "quarter" and "month" for the same $90,000.
improvement_opportunities: State the return assumption and show the three-line arithmetic ($158,800 in; at 10% about $290,600 out) then reframe the title, e.g. "$90,000 a Year at 40: What You Would Really Need".
Rework the tax scene with the 0%/15% stack ($3,720) and say which distributions are qualified.
Correct the tickers (SPYI, QQQI) and state their tax characterisation from the fund documents.
Match the thumbnail to the quiet-life message (coffee, same apartment, phone notification).
